prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1269; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The claim was logged after the policyholder reported a collision at an intersection while turning left, and the claimant, who is not represented by counsel, was assigned to the file for injury review.
Entry 2: The driver is listed on the policy and the policy was in force at the time of loss, with nothing indicating the damage predated the coverage start.
Entry 3: Police records and statements from the scene confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of impact, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior file history.
Entry 4: Scene photographs confirm several details of the impact, though no independent witnesses have come forward to describe how the collision happened.
Entry 5: The claimant reports a wrist fracture, and the kind of injury and the force of the crash appear consistent with one another based on the photos and the vehicle damage pattern.
Entry 6: No earlier injury to the same area of the body is known from the claimant's records, and the claimant has given the same account of events in every conversation so far.
Entry 7: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this type of fracture, and the medical timeline is being reviewed against the reported mechanism.
Entry 8: It remains unclear whether all of the vehicle damage resulted from this single impact, so the repair estimate is being checked line by line against the photographs.
Entry 9: The file is being held for the adjuster's review of the medical reports and the damage assessment before any settlement position is considered.
